title: European sidemen; practicing with records and tapes
summary: Players from France and Afghanistan swung, and he practices with records and tapes.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you play with European musicians over there?
Yeah, we had a couple of guys. Let's see, one was from France -- a bass player, and then they have another guy from Afghanistan. They couldn't speak no English, but they could play.
Was their playing any different from Americans?
No, I mean, swing-- they'd listen to records, you know. That's why its good to get a record that you like and listen to it and put it on tape and keep it around.
Do you do that much? You mentioned earlier that you didn't do that earlier.
No there wasn't no tapes. We had a thing out called a wire tape. I couldn't even afford that.
Do you listen to recordings now, or have you in the past.

No I listen to them in order to practice. I have a couple of types of Jimmy Rushing and its got a huge variety of songs-- a couple of albums. And I can practice with that-- put it on my amplifier and turn it up and its like a big band, you know. I even recorded some things with a big band playing and I'm-- I had it fixed up so I could play right along with 'em. And it came out good. Sound like I'm playin' with them.
